clippings.speaker: Akira Kurosawa
clippings.quote: Mifune had a kind of talent I had never encountered before… He reacts so swiftly to direction; if I say one thing to him, he understands 10. The ordinary Japanese actor might need 10 feet of film to get across an impression: Mifune needed only 3 feet … I decided to turn him loose.
clippings.title: Toshiro Mifune dead at 77
clippings.context: Variety's obituary of Mifune quoting Kurosawa's autobiography (Something Like an Autobiography, English translation) on their first film together.

clippings.speaker: Akira Kurosawa
clippings.quote: His sense of timing was the keenest I had ever seen in a Japanese actor… And yet with all his quickness, he also had surprisingly fine sensibilities.
clippings.title: Toshiro Mifune dead at 77
clippings.context: Continuation of the autobiography passage quoted in Variety's obituary of Mifune; translated from Japanese.

clippings.speaker: Akira Kurosawa
clippings.quote: I'm not usually impressed by actors, but Mifune impressed me. If I tell him one thing, he understands ten… If I had to think of a flaw, the only thing I can come up with is his voice is a little rough and sometimes it's hard to understand.
clippings.title: Seven Samurai (1954)
clippings.context: TCM article by Rob Nixon quoting Kurosawa's memoirs (a different translation of the autobiography passage).

clippings.speaker: Akira Kurosawa
clippings.quote: a young man reeling around the room in a violent frenzy. It was as frightening as watching a wounded beast trying to break loose. I was transfixed
clippings.title: Why did Toshiro Mifune fall out with Akira Kurosawa?
clippings.context: Kurosawa recalling first seeing Mifune at Toho's 1946 new-faces audition; originally from his autobiography, quoted without citation.

clippings.speaker: Toshirō Mifune
clippings.quote: Yes, on Yojimbo… One day Kurosawa said, 'I won't mention names, but the actors are late.' I said, 'What are you talking about? I'm the actor.' Every day after that, when Kurosawa arrived, I would be there already, in costume and makeup from 6 a.m. I showed him.
clippings.title: Film Review: A Perfunctory Documentary on Toshiro Mifune
clippings.context: Mifune answering critic Gerald Peary in a 1985 Montreal hotel interview, asked whether he and Kurosawa ever quarreled; recounted in Peary's 2016 review.

clippings.speaker: Toshirō Mifune
clippings.quote: No matter how much I drank the night before, I never once was late on his films. But with Kurosawa, sometimes people are waiting, and he never shows up. The people go to his house, and he says, 'I'm sorry. I don't feel well today.'
clippings.title: Film Review: A Perfunctory Documentary on Toshiro Mifune
clippings.context: Same 1985 interview with Gerald Peary, two decades after their last film together.

clippings.speaker: Toshirō Mifune
clippings.quote: I have never as an actor done anything that I am proud of other than with him.
clippings.title: Why did Toshiro Mifune fall out with Akira Kurosawa?
clippings.context: Mifune's widely repeated tribute after the split; Far Out gives no source (other sites trace it to Donald Richie's The Films of Akira Kurosawa).

notes: No firsthand Kurosawa interview on Mifune found openly; his side relies on the autobiography as quoted by Variety/TCM/Far Out. UPI 1984 Mifune interview blocked to curl and had no Kurosawa quotes; Far Out quotes are unsourced.
